title: How AI Communication Strategies Influence Corporate Evaluation and Investment Intention: An Experimental Study
affiliations: , , , Independent, University of Florida - Warrington College of Business Administration and University of Science and Technology of China (USTC)

detail.title: How AI Communication Strategies Influence Corporate Evaluation and Investment Intention: An Experimental Study
detail.abstract: As firms rapidly embed AI into products, operations, and strategies, they are increasingly judged not only by what AI they build, but by how credibly they communicate about it. Yet AI information is complex and can be easily misunderstood, and public attention to AI washing and overpromising can quickly trigger skepticism, directly harming corporate evaluation and investment decisions. Despite the growing prevalence and high stakes of AI-related disclosures, we know little about which AI communication strategies help firms earn investment. Based on the accessibility-diagnosticity theory (ADT), we developed a framework that distinguishes between two AI communication strategies: engagement and responsiveness. We recruited 320 investors for a 2×2 between-subjects experiment and found that, compared with the responsiveness strategy, the engagement AI communication strategy led to more positive corporate evaluations and higher investment intentions, with these effects mediated by increased AI association and reduced AI skepticism. We further found that the effects of AI communication strategies were stronger for AI-newcomer firms than for AI-experienced firms. This study contributes to the fields of AI and firm communication research by exploring how AI communication strategies influence stakeholder responses.

title: Dynamic Driver Compartmentalization Using On-Demand Memory Domains
affiliations: , LMU - Ludwig Maximilians Universität Munich and LMU - Ludwig Maximilians Universität Munich

detail.title: Dynamic Driver Compartmentalization Using On-Demand Memory Domains
detail.abstract: Device drivers contribute disproportionately to kernel vulnerabilities due to their large attack surface. This work proposes an on-demand driver compartmentalization mechanism that assigns temporary memory domains to active driver routines. Using lightweight memory remapping and PKS-controlled regions, the approach confines driver faults without interrupting global kernel execution. Evaluated across 14 commodity drivers, the system prevents privilege-escalation exploits in 11 CVEs and contains the impact of remaining attacks. Performance overhead stays within 4.1% on I/O-intensive workloads. This dynamic model demonstrates an effective balance between strong isolation and operational flexibility.

title: Dual-Layer Isolation for eBPF Execution Using PKS Memory Sandboxing and Verified Call Policies
affiliations: Nanyang Technological University, Singapore, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore and Nanyang Technological University, Singapore

detail.title: Dual-Layer Isolation for eBPF Execution Using PKS Memory Sandboxing and Verified Call Policies
detail.abstract: eBPF programs run inside the kernel and pose security risks if verifier gaps are exploited. We introduce a dual-layer isolation mechanism where PKS-enforced memory domains confine eBPF runtime state while a verified call-policy engine restricts privileged helper use. Experiments using 120 real-world eBPF programs and 9 exploit PoCs show that the system neutralizes all tested memory-corruption vectors and blocks unsafe helper chains. Runtime overhead is below 6% for packet-processing workloads. This approach strengthens kernel security without limiting eBPF flexibility.

title: Fine-Grained Kernel Memory Isolation Using Hardware Protection Keys and Capability Mapping
affiliations: Kyoto University of Advanced Science - Kyoto Kameoka Campus, Kyoto University of Advanced Science - Kyoto Kameoka Campus and Kyoto University of Advanced Science - Kyoto Kameoka Campus

detail.title: Fine-Grained Kernel Memory Isolation Using Hardware Protection Keys and Capability Mapping
detail.abstract: Hardware protection keys (PKU/PKS) offer lightweight mechanisms for runtime memory access control, yet prior systems often apply them at coarse granularity. We introduce a capability-mapped isolation framework that partitions kernel subsystems into fine-grained memory regions with adaptive key assignments. Tested on Linux 6.1, the system enforces per-function memory boundaries with <3.5% performance overhead, blocking 94% of simulated invalid-write attacks. Stress tests using 22 historical CVE exploits demonstrate complete mitigation in 18 cases. Our results show that combining capability mapping with PKS significantly strengthens kernel memory integrity while remaining deployment-friendly.

title: Three Strategic Bets on AI's Future

detail.title: Three Strategic Bets on AI's Future

declarations.funderStatement: This work is not funded

detail.abstract: Every major LLM launch we tracked coincided with total market growth and showed little evidence of cannibalization between models. When OpenAI releases a new model, Claude's user base grows. When Anthropic releases a new model, ChatGPT's user base grows. The "AI war" zero-sum framing appears to be incorrect. Three radically different monetization strategies are succeeding at once. ChatGPT pursues scale: around 79% market share with moderate revenue per user. Google Gemini pursues ecosystem: 12% share but almost no direct revenue, effectively subsidizing AI through its other businesses. Claude pursues premium: under 1% share but 40x higher revenue per user than Gemini. Each strategy faces different risks, but all three seem viable, at least for now. As market growth slows or capital markets become less forgiving, these strategies face different vulnerabilities. Scale leaders must convert free users. Ecosystem players must justify subsidies. Premium players must stay differentiated. Executives building, buying, or investing in AI should resist single-outcome bets and instead match strategy to structural advantage.

title: Multilingual Bias in Large Language Models

detail.title: Multilingual Bias in Large Language Models
detail.abstract: This study investigates multilingual bias and toxicity in large language models (LLMs), focusing on ChatGPT 3.5-turbo. The research addresses two key questions: (1) the intrinsic bias and toxicity features within individual languages, and (2) the comparative differences in bias and toxicity across different languages. Using a novel methodology that employs DeepSeek-Chat as a judge to rank generated texts, the study evaluates bias and toxicity across 13 languages, including both high-resource and low-resource languages. The Iterative Luce Spectral Ranking (ILSR) algorithm is applied to generate ranking weights, which are then analyzed using Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression to identify significant variables influencing bias and toxicity. Key findings reveal that prompt style significantly impacts bias and toxicity, with direct prompts generating more biased and toxic content compared to emotional or cautious prompts. Omitting age and nationality information increases bias and toxicity, while omitting gender reduces it. Female-related content is more biased and toxic across languages, and Russian-related topics exhibit higher levels of bias and toxicity. Low-resource languages, such as Mongolian and Burmese, show the highest levels of bias and toxicity, likely due to underdeveloped corpora. In contrast, East Asian languages exhibit high bias but low toxicity, while European languages show mediumlow bias and higher toxicity. English, as a high-resource language, demonstrates low bias and medium toxicity. The study concludes that prompt style plays a dominant role in shaping bias and toxicity across languages, suggesting that incorporating cautious language in prompts can mitigate these issues. The findings provide valuable insights for developers and tuners aiming to reduce bias and toxicity in multilingual LLMs, emphasizing the importance of prompt design and the differential effects of omitted information.

title: Formal Verification of PKS-Based Kernel Isolation Policies Using State Transition Models
affiliations: Indian Institute of Science (IISc) - Department of Computational and Data Science, Indian Institute of Science (IISc) - Department of Computational and Data Science and Indian Institute of Science (IISc) - Department of Computational and Data Science

detail.title: Formal Verification of PKS-Based Kernel Isolation Policies Using State Transition Models
detail.abstract: We present a formal verification framework for PKS-governed isolation rules in the kernel. A state-transition model is derived from kernel memory-access traces and checked against safety invariants using SMT solvers. On nine Linux subsystems, verification identifies 17 incorrect permission transitions in prototype isolation policies. After correction, the formally verified policy withstands all 28 injected attack attempts, demonstrating improved correctness. Overhead for model extraction and checking remains acceptable for offline validation workflows. This work shows that formal reasoning can significantly improve the reliability of kernel compartmentalization.

title: Unexpected Monetary Incentives and User-Generated Content on Digital Platforms
affiliations: Tilburg University - Tilburg University School of Economics and Management, Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST) - Department of Information Systems, Business Statistics and Operations Management and University of Basel - Faculty of Business and Economics

detail.title: Unexpected Monetary Incentives and User-Generated Content on Digital Platforms

publicationDetails.journalName: HKUST Business School Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Tournament schemes are increasingly adopted to incentivize the production of user-generated content (UGC) on digital platforms. Identifying the causal effect of tournaments is challenging due to self-selected participation. We address this challenge using a proprietary data set from three European deal-sharing platforms that implemented a daily tournament, which rewarded the top-voted contributions in each category. We leverage the scheme's undisclosed rollouts-users became aware of it only after winning-as a staggered treatment. Using a difference-indifferences (DID) identification strategy, we find that, after their first reward, users posted 14% more deals and increased their upvoting and downvoting behaviors by 8.5% and 11% respectively. The incentive amplified motivation mostly among an extrinsicallydriven subgroup of repeated winners, whereas the majority of other rewarded users remain unaffected. These repeated winners sabotaged others by casting more downvotes on competing contributions, thereby distorting the platforms' quality signals. We observe an asymmetric shift in content production toward mainstream categories. We attribute this shift to structural constraints that limit the scalability of volume-based strategies in niche markets. We discuss implications for the design of tournament schemes on digital platforms.

title: Information Privilege and the Politics of Translating "Depression"
affiliations: , Lyceum of the Philippines University and Lyceum of the Philippines University

detail.title: Information Privilege and the Politics of Translating "Depression"
detail.abstract: Information privilege helps us see how access and visibility shape what becomes credible, legitimate, and shareable knowledge. It refers not only to unequal access to information, often structured by institutional affiliation, education, class, or social position, but also to unequal access to the means of making experience intelligible. In scholarly communication, this usually appears through paywalls, subscriptions, databases, and prestige economies. Yet information privilege also operates through language. As discussions from the Association of College & Research Libraries have suggested, access to information is inseparable from access to the systems that authorize what counts as legitimate knowledge.

title: Breaking Down Language Barriers to Reduce Information Privilege in Scholarly Communication

detail.title: Breaking Down Language Barriers to Reduce Information Privilege in Scholarly Communication
detail.abstract: For decades, English has been a lingua franca in the research community, where it has become the principal language for publishing and conferences. But when one main language is used to share information, knowledge of this language is also needed to access information. In this way, English has become linked to information privilege: people who have mastered English can access scholarly information more easily than people who are less comfortable in this language. This has ripple effects, influencing the extent to which scientists can participate fully in scholarly communication. While the problems are clear, the solutions are trickier.

title: Rethinking the Customer-Banker Relationship: Advancing the Argument for Magistrate Courts Jurisdiction, for Faster Justice

detail.title: Rethinking the Customer-Banker Relationship: Advancing the Argument for Magistrate Courts Jurisdiction, for Faster Justice

declarations.ethicsApproval: Original thoughts of the author. Not plagiarized.

detail.abstract: The question as to which court has jurisdiction in a customer/banker relationship is one that has been decided issues in Nigeria`s case laws; with it being settled law that the Federal and State High courts being the courts in question. What if were the case that, when it comes to customer/banker relationships, the magistrate court have jurisdiction; will this create an effective structure for resolution of these disputes? This article intends to answer this question. This article examines the delicate but fundamental issue of jurisdiction in customer and banker disputes in Nigeria. It begins from the settled principle that jurisdiction is the life wire of any court and must be clearly derived from constitutional and statutory provisions. Furthermore, it explains the contractual nature of the customer banker relationship, relying on statutory definitions and case law to show that such disputes are essentially personal actions arising from contract. The constitutional framework, particularly section 251(1)(d) of the 1999 Constitution, together with judicial authorities, is analysed to clarify that both the Federal High Court and State High Courts exercise jurisdiction in these matters. In addition, the article advances the argument that Magistrate Courts, by virtue of existing Magistrates' Court Laws, can and should exercise jurisdiction over individual customer banker disputes within their monetary limits. Furthermore, nothing in the Constitution expressly excludes them from doing so. Beyond the legal argument, the paper contends that many of these disputes involve modest sums and urgent financial concerns, yet take years to resolve in already congested High Courts. Therefore, recognising or clearly legislating Magistrate Court jurisdiction would promote faster resolution, reduce pressure on superior courts, and strengthen access to justice for the ordinary citizen.

title: Understanding Product Satisfaction in E-commerce: Insights from Online Reviews of Activewear
affiliations: Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University, Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University and Georgia Southern University

detail.title: Understanding Product Satisfaction in E-commerce: Insights from Online Reviews of Activewear
detail.abstract: Understanding the factors influencing consumer satisfaction in online consumer reviews (OCRs) is critical as this market grows with e-commerce and OCRs are excellent predictors of consumer satisfaction and buying behavior. This study explores key features of activewear OCRs in relation to satisfaction using machine learning techniques, including topic modeling and sentiment analyses, and regression analysis. A set of broad categories, inferred from previous studies, serves as the conceptual framework for grouping the major topics. After collecting, cleaning, and preprocessing data, 2,300 OCRs were analyzed, revealing ten key themes: expectations, perceived product performance in functional, expressive, aesthetic, and extrinsic dimensions, perceived service performance, dis/confirmation, dis/satisfaction, dis/satisfaction outcomes, and descriptive information. Positive sentiments dominated themes like expectations, expressive and aesthetic product performance, satisfaction, and recommendation, while perceived service quality and extrinsic product performance had neutral to negative sentiments. Regression analyses showed that satisfaction was positively related to all four dimensions of perceived product performance, perceived service quality performance, dis/confirmation, and dis/satisfaction outcomes. This study offers valuable theoretical and practical implications for improving consumer satisfaction with activewear.

title: The Universal Pursuit of Safety and the Demand for (Lethal, Non-Lethal or No) Guns
affiliations: Harvard University - Harvard Kennedy School (HKS), Harvard University and Harvard University - Department of Economics

detail.title: The Universal Pursuit of Safety and the Demand for (Lethal, Non-Lethal or No) Guns
detail.abstract:
Lethal firearm ownership is deeply polarizing in the United States. We show that beneath this polarization, owners and non-owners share a common objective — safety — but disagree sharply about whether lethal firearms achieve it. Using an original survey of more than 5,400 respondents combined with randomized experiments, we document that owners feel safe and confident with firearms, while non-owners on balance feel less safe around them and perceive large private costs and social harms. Demand for lethal firearms is nonetheless potentially large and growing: one-third of non-owners express interest in acquiring one — these individuals report the lowest day-to-day safety — while very few owners would consider reducing their holdings. Persuading owners to relinquish firearms without any replacement appears unrealistic; the more tractable margins may be safe storage and non-lethal substitution for additional purchases. We organize these patterns through a framework centered on a perceived safety possibilities frontier (SPF) — the safety outcomes a household believes achievable with different combinations of lethal and non-lethal tools. Households may differ in firearm demand because they face different risk environments, weigh protective benefits against harms differently, or hold different beliefs about the frontier. Our descriptive evidence points to heterogeneous beliefs as important drivers, suggesting that levers such as information could shift the perceived frontier. These patterns motivate three experimental treatments: one on the private legal/medical costs of lethal firearm ownership, and two on a non-lethal firearm (NLFA), with and without a conservative pundit’s endorsement. The private-cost treatment increases concern about harms among all respondents and support for safe storage policies, and modestly raises stated willingness to keep lethal firearms locked. NLFA treatments raise willingness to pay for an NLFA, to keep lethal firearms locked, and support for incapacitating over lethal firearms and for policies encouraging NLFAs. These effects are largely persistent. Importantly, NLFA information does not increase willingness to reduce lethal firearm ownership but does increase willingness to store lethal firearms safely. Our results suggest that many owners perceive the SPF differently from nonowners, neglecting harms or less-lethal alternatives, yet remain open to such tools. Overall, individuals share a common goal — safety — yet disagree about the means. Although these disagreements appear entrenched, people remain receptive to alternatives that might command broader agreement.

title: Towards Economic Diversification in Macao SAR
affiliations: Banco de España

detail.title: Towards Economic Diversification in Macao SAR
detail.abstract: Macao SAR has embarked on an ambitious economic diversification strategy aimed at reducing its reliance on gaming and fostering sustainable long-term growth. The government’s plan targets the development of four nascent industries—scientific and technological research, traditional Chinese medicine, tourism and convention services, and modern financial services—complemented by the upgrading of the broader tourism and leisure sector. Central to this strategy is deeper integration with the Greater Bay Area (GBA), particularly through the Guangdong-Macao Intensive Cooperation Zone (GMICZ) and the development of the Special Economic Zone (SEZ) in Hengqin. Given Macao SAR’s high population density and limited land availability, Hengqin—offering substantially larger territory and lower population density—provides a structural opportunity to alleviate spatial constraints and support industrial expansion.This Selected Issues paper assesses the feasibility and potential gains of Macao SAR’s diversification strategy using product-level export counterpart data to evaluate the territory’s underlying productive knowledge and know-how. The analysis first characterizes the distinctive features of Macao SAR’s export basket. It then measures the distance between Macao SAR’s existing productive capabilities and those required for the government’s targeted industries. The paper further examines Guangdong’s productive knowledge base to identify complementarities and cross-regional synergies that could accelerate diversification within the GBA framework. Based on these findings, the study derives policy implications to strengthen the effectiveness of Macao SAR’s diversification efforts, including targeted industrial policies, cross-border collaboration mechanisms, and strategic use of the Hengqin SEZ as a platform for capability upgrading and structural transformation.

title: A Forecast Model For Crypto Currencies
affiliations: Northeastern University (USA) and John P. Stevens High School

detail.title: A Forecast Model For Crypto Currencies
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether the well known equity momentum effect exists in cryptocurrency markets. We estimate daily cross-sectional regressions of forward returns on past returns with daily price data from Binance for about 50 most actively traded cryptocurrencies. The resulting time series of regression coefficients serves as a measure of the momentum effect's strength and evolution over time. With the results, we propose a dollar-neutral trading strategy that goes long the top quartile and short the bottom quartile of cryptocurrencies ranked by their momentum signal. Our historical simulation shows the strategy has better sharpe ratio and drawdown profile than simply buying and holding Bitcoin alone.

title: Work from Home and Fertility
affiliations: Stanford University, University College London, ITAM - Business School, Stanford University - Department of Economics, Stanford University, Ifo Institute and Princeton University

detail.title: Work from Home and Fertility
detail.abstract:
We investigate how fertility relates to work from home (WFH) in the post-pandemic era, drawing on original data from our Global Survey of Working Arrangements and U.S. Survey of Working Arrangements and Attitudes. Realized fertility from 2023 to 2025 and future planned fertility are higher among adults who WFH at least one day a week and, for couples, higher yet when both partners do so. Estimated lifetime fertility is greater by 0.32 children per woman when both partners WFH one or more days per week as compared to the case where neither does. The implications for national fertility rates differ across countries due mainly to large differences in WFH rates. In a complementary analysis using other U.S. data before and after the pandemic, one-year fertility rates rise with WFH opportunities in one's own occupation and, for couples, in the partner's occupation.

title: Energy Transition and Labour Market Resilience: Evidence from EU Member States, 2000–2024
affiliations: 1 Decembrie 1918 University of Alba Iulia

detail.title: Energy Transition and Labour Market Resilience: Evidence from EU Member States, 2000–2024
detail.abstract: The transition toward low-carbon energy systems represents one of the most profound structural transformations affecting modern economies. Beyond environmental and technological implications, energy transition may also influence labour market dynamics through sectoral reallocation, energy cost shocks, and structural adjustment processes. This paper investigates how energy transition and structural composition shape labour market resilience across European Union Member States over the period 2000–2024.Using a panel dataset for EU-27 countries and a two-way fixed effects framework with country-clustered standard errors, we analyze both long-run structural relationships and crisis-specific amplification mechanisms during the Global Financial Crisis and the COVID-19 shock. Energy transition is captured through energy intensity, renewable energy consumption, and carbon emissions, while structural exposure is measured through sectoral employment composition.The results show that higher energy intensity is associated with greater labour market vulnerability during systemic shocks, while renewable energy expansion is linked to modest improvements in labour market stability. Sectoral employment structure also plays an important role: economies with larger industrial employment shares experience stronger unemployment amplification, whereas service-oriented structures display greater resilience. Human capital further mitigates crisis-induced labour market deterioration.Heterogeneity analysis reveals significant differences between EU-15 and EU-13 countries, suggesting that the labour market consequences of energy transition depend on development stage and structural legacy. Overall, the findings indicate that labour market resilience in Europe is closely intertwined with the pace and structure of energy transition.

title: When Income Support Hurts and Helps: Health Effects of Survivors Benefits
affiliations: Purdue University and Purdue University

detail.title: When Income Support Hurts and Helps: Health Effects of Survivors Benefits
detail.abstract: How does income support after widowhood affect health over the life cycle? To answer this question, we study Social Security Survivors Benefits, which become available to widowed individuals at age 60 in the United States. Using a fuzzy regression discontinuity design with Health and Retirement Study data, we find that eligibility reduces selfreported good health and increases diabetes diagnoses in the short run, with effects concentrated among financially dependent widows. These effects are not explained by changes in medical utilization but coincide with increased food expenditures, suggesting a consumption-based mechanism. To examine longer-run consequences, we exploit the 1965 reform that lowered the eligibility age from 65 to 60 and use cohort mortality data to compare cohorts with different exposure durations. We find that expanded eligibility improves survival to age 70. Descriptive cause-of-death patterns indicate larger mortality declines from cardiovascular disease, tuberculosis, and suicide in high-widow-prevalence states. Together, the results suggest that income support can generate short-run health risks while improving longer-run survival.

title: Laughing Matters: How Profound Humor Exposes the Fault Lines of Human Understanding
affiliations: City University of New York (CUNY) - Koppelman School of Business and City University of New York (CUNY) - Paul H. Chook Department of Information Systems & Statistics

detail.title: Laughing Matters: How Profound Humor Exposes the Fault Lines of Human Understanding
detail.abstract: Although often dismissed as mere entertainment, sophisticated comedy serves as a rigorous vehicle for philosophical inquiry. This paper introduces a taxonomy of profound humor, defined as comedy that transcends simple amusement to engage fundamental questions of existence, ethics, and identity. By analyzing hundreds of examples drawn from philosophy, religion, psychology, politics, and everyday life, we identify seven primary categories. These categories include: • Epistemological humor, which exposes the fragility of knowledge. • Paradoxical humor, which uses logical contradiction to generate insight. • Linguistic and semantic humor, which exploits the instabilities of language. • Philosophical humor, which playfully engages the ideas of major thinkers. • Existential and metaphysical humor, which confronts mortality and the nature of reality. • Self-referential humor, which turns the comedic gaze inward. • Socio-ethical humor, which lays bare moral failures and ideological biases. We argue that profound humor functions much like philosophy by disrupting habitual thought and forcing a cognitive reframing. Drawing on Arthur Koestler's concept of bisociation, we propose that profound humor is distinguished from ordinary comedy by its productive irresolution. In these instances, the punchline opens onto a genuine fault line in human understanding rather than simply dissolving tension. Because the insights generated by profound jokes linger long after the laughter subsides, this taxonomy establishes a robust foundation for using humor as a specialized tool for education, social critique, and deep philosophical engagement.

title: Predictive Intelligence: A Canonical Organizational Paradigm Beyond Artificial Intelligence

detail.title: Predictive Intelligence: A Canonical Organizational Paradigm Beyond Artificial Intelligence
detail.abstract:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become the dominant umbrella construct in contemporary management and information systems research. However, as AI increasingly encompasses systems that generate predictions, recommendations, and decisions, its explanatory precision for organizational performance diminishes. This article argues that AI is a technological paradigm, not an organizational one. Competitive advantage does not stem from algorithmic capability alone, but from the institutionalized capacity to transform calibrated predictions into precision-governed action.

We introduce Predictive Intelligence (PI) as a distinct organizational paradigm. PI is defined as the organizational capability to (1) generate calibrated, context-grounded probabilistic expectations, (2) translate these expectations into ranked next-best-actions with explicit estimated precision predictions (EPP), and (3) institutionalize feedback mechanisms that measurably improve decision precision over time.

Building on bounded rationality (Simon, 1955), behavioral decision theory (Kahneman & Tversky, 1979), exploration–exploitation theory (March, 1991), predictive analytics research (Shmueli & Koppius, 2011), and dynamic capabilities theory (Teece et al., 1997), we derive ten theoretical propositions, articulate boundary conditions, and propose a formal decision architecture model. We position PI as a sovereignty paradigm over uncertainty, replacing “AI adoption” as the primary explanatory construct in organizational research.

title: IEEPA's Changing Context, Multipolar Sanctions, and the Evolving Limits of Economic Security
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) - Faculty of Law

detail.title: IEEPA's Changing Context, Multipolar Sanctions, and the Evolving Limits of Economic Security

publicationDetails.detailsText: IEEPA's Changing Context, Multipolar Sanctions, and the Evolving Limits of Economic Security, 78 Rutgers University Law Review (forthcoming 2026)

detail.abstract: The International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA), originally conceived as a tool of calibrated sanctions against extraordinary foreign threats, has become the statutory basis for an expanding arsenal of economic statecraft. While courts have generally deferred to expansive invocations of the statute, this has recently been rejected by the Supreme Court in Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump with respect to IEEPA's novel application to tariffs. At the same time, this and related judgments have been framed narrowly, and have so far declined to address in detail (including as a "major question") the limits of IEEPA's purpose or any role of international law norms in contextualizing its grant of Executive authority. This Article seeks, first, to supply that context by interrogating IEEPA's transformation as part of a broader trajectory in which security discourses deformalize express statutory boundaries, displace Congressional control, and create growing dissonance between U.S. foreign policy and acknowledged obligations under international law. Subsequently, via close scrutiny of evolving state practice, opinio juris, and jurisprudence, the Article demonstrates that unilateral sanctions which generate systemic insecurity for other states may contravene norms of non-intervention, sovereign equality, and humanitarian protection. Finally, the Article further contextualizes U.S. sanctions practice within the emerging multipolar sanctions environment, in which powers such as China, the European Union, and Russia, among others, also increasingly deploy unilateral coercive measures in a competing and mutually-influencing manner. On this basis, the Article identifies an ongoing process of social construction in global society in which rival visions of "economic security" are contested.

title: Examination Of The Effects Of Authentic Leadership On Knowledge Management, Organizational Identification, And Emotional Commitment

detail.title: Examination Of The Effects Of Authentic Leadership On Knowledge Management, Organizational Identification, And Emotional Commitment
detail.abstract: The rapid change and development in various sectors make it crucial for organizations to manage their knowledge and share this information with their employees in order to adapt. Employees' experience, along with their identification with the organization, is a significant factor in achieving higher performance. Employees' emotional attachment to their organization eliminates the idea of leaving, which is considered a significant advantage for organizations. Employees' ability to perform above expectations within organizations is directly proportional to the impact of the leadership roles held by senior managers. The positive influence of leadership roles on employees is important both in terms of commitment and their identification with the organization.

title: From Scarcity to Abundance: Academic Knowledge Production in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
affiliations: Deakin University and University of Queensland

detail.title: From Scarcity to Abundance: Academic Knowledge Production in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
detail.abstract: The institutional architecture of modern academia rests on scarcity: research is costly to produce, slow to publish, and difficult to evaluate. Artificial intelligence is dismantling this logic. Drawing on recent empirical evidence showing that AI-assisted researchers produce 50-60% more papers, that AI-generated content pervades up to one-fifth of publications in some fields, and that autonomous AI research systems are in active development, this essay argues that academic knowledge is transitioning from scarcity to abundance. We contend this transition will be as consequential for scholarship as the digital revolution was for media. To navigate it, we propose a three-layer framework for the post-scarcity knowledge economy: Layer 1 (Generation), where AI systems produce research at scale; Layer 2 (Filtration), where AI curates output for domain specialists; and Layer 3 (Epistemic Governance), where human academics serve as the scarce resource in an abundant system, formulating consequential questions, exercising ethical judgment, interpreting findings in context, and directing the research agenda. When production becomes abundant, value migrates to governance. The academy must proactively redesign its institutions around this new value locus before AI renders its current structures obsolete.

title: Arbitration and the Commodification of Justice
affiliations: King's College London

detail.title: Arbitration and the Commodification of Justice
detail.abstract: This paper examines what happens when justice is commodified. Not privatised; commodified. Privatisation concerns where adjudication is located and how it is governed; commodification concerns the criteria through which justice is valued, evaluated, and justified. Arbitration offers a particularly clear example to observe a broader transformation in contemporary legal life: justice increasingly understood not as a public institutional practice, but as a service defined by performance, expertise, responsiveness, flexibility, and user satisfaction. Arbitration’s familiar virtues are not merely procedural advantages; they are also standards through which justice itself is revalued.

title: Examination Of The Effects Of Despotic Leadership And Strategic Human Resources Management On Intention To Leave And Job Satisfaction

detail.title: Examination Of The Effects Of Despotic Leadership And Strategic Human Resources Management On Intention To Leave And Job Satisfaction
detail.abstract: In the highly competitive business environment, organizations implement human resources policies and practices aimed at increasing employee motivation and performance. The effort to minimize employee turnover is directly proportional to employee satisfaction and their desire to remain with the organization. The ever-increasing performance of organizations is evident as a result of the leadership roles of senior executives and the human resources policies implemented. Employee dissatisfaction, the attitudes and behaviors of leaders towards employees, and the implemented human resources policies also determine the lifespan of organizations. Studies in these areas are crucial in contributing to the decision-making of senior executives and the development of leadership roles within organizations.

title: From Digital Desire to Algorithmic Control: Libidinal Economy, Simulacra, and the Political Economy of the Avatar

detail.title: From Digital Desire to Algorithmic Control: Libidinal Economy, Simulacra, and the Political Economy of the Avatar
detail.abstract: This paper examines the transformation of libidinal exchange in the context of platform capitalism, where intimacy and self-presentation are increasingly mediated through digital avatars and algorithmically curated environments. Drawing on Jean-François Lyotard's libidinal economy, Michel Foucault's disciplinary societies, Gilles Deleuze's societies of control and deterritorialisation, and Jean Baudrillard's theory of simulacra, the analysis situates contemporary forms of a digital simulacrum of a romantic relationship, facilitated through app-based virtual dating-the monetisation of attention, affect, and symbolic self-replication-within a broader economic-philosophical framework. Žižek's notion of the-digital unconscious‖ provides a critical lens for understanding how responsibility, desire, and symbolic castration are reconfigured when subjectivity is externalised into AI-mediated interactions. In dialogue with Knightian uncertainty and its ontological implications, the paper argues that the trade in self-as-avatar represents a mutation in the relationship between future-oriented action and libidinal investment. Rather than dissolving uncertainty, algorithmic mediation reframes it as a productive force, embedding affective economies into the logics of prediction and control. This hybridisation of economic rationality and libidinal circulation raises fundamental questions for the philosophy of economics, ethics, and the possibility of post-capitalist futures.

title: Refugee Logistics: Camps and Beyond
affiliations: Simon Fraser University (SFU) - Beedie School of Business

detail.title: Refugee Logistics: Camps and Beyond

publicationDetails.detailsText: This is a pre-print version before the editorial process. To see & cite the published version, Sahinyazan, F. (2025). Refugee logistics: camps and beyond. In G. Kovács and N. Altay (Eds) A Research Agenda for Humanitarian Logistics (pp. 71-90). Edward Elgar Publishing.

detail.abstract: This book chapter explores the complexities of refugee logistics and humanitarian operations, highlighting the crucial role of supply chain management in addressing the needs of displaced populations, including innovative approaches to camp operations, urban refugee integration, and the provision of essential services such as education and healthcare. The chapter emphasizes the importance of collaboration between humanitarian organizations, local actors, and the use of cutting-edge technology to enhance efficiency and sustainability in aid delivery. Through a blend of case studies and theoretical insights, it offers a roadmap for improving the well-being and dignity of refugees, advocating for solutions that not only meet immediate needs but also foster long-term resilience and integration. This work seeks to inspire further research and action in the field of humanitarian logistics, urging a reimagined approach that views refugees as active participants in their journey towards stability and self-sufficiency.

title: How National Institutional Configurations Shape the Global Diffusion of B Corp Certification
affiliations: University of Luxembourg - Interdisciplinary Centre for Security, Reliability and Trust (SnT), University of Luxembourg - Interdisciplinary Centre for Security, Reliability and Trust (SnT) and University of Trier - Faculty of Management

detail.title: How National Institutional Configurations Shape the Global Diffusion of B Corp Certification

keywords: Business Strategy and the Environment B Corp certification

detail.abstract: Drawing on institutional theory, we examine how distinct forms of national-level normative pressures shape the global diffusion of B Corp certification, a leading voluntary sustainability standard. We differentiate policy-driven, information-driven, and environment-driven pressures arising from climate policy, sustainable movement organizations (SMOs), and natural disasters, respectively. Using panel data on 9,796 initial B Corp certifications across 92 countries from 2007 to 2023, we test how these pressures independently and jointly influence certification uptake worldwide. We find that each pressure is positively associated with diffusion. However, environmental turbulence weakens the positive association between policy-driven pressure and certification uptake, while the influence of information-driven pressure remains robust under such conditions. These findings point to institutional reconfiguration under environmental turbulence: disruptions do not uniformly intensify institutional pressures but instead shift which actors shape adoption, dampening regulatory momentum while leaving information-driven pressures largely intact. By disaggregating normative pressures into stakeholder-specific mechanisms, we enrich institutional theory by explaining how environmental turbulence reshapes the drivers of global B Corp certification diffusion.

title: A Solicit-Then-Suggest Model of Agentic Purchasing
affiliations: University of Toronto - Rotman School of Management and University of Toronto - Rotman School of Management

detail.title: A Solicit-Then-Suggest Model of Agentic Purchasing

publicationDetails.detailsText: Rotman School of Management Working Paper (forthcoming)
publicationDetails.journalName: University of Toronto - Rotman School of Management Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: The e-commerce landscape is undergoing a fundamental shift from search-based shopping to agentic purchasing. AI shopping agents are replacing keyword search with multi-round conversations, in which the agent learns what customers want through targeted questions and then presents a tailored assortment of recommendations. We develop the solicit-then-suggest framework to model this emerging paradigm of agentic purchasing. An agent conducts $m$ rounds of targeted solicitation in a $d$-dimensional preference space to progressively refine its belief about the customer's ideal product, and then recommends $k$ products from which the customer selects. We identify the economic forces shaping this new form of e-commerce. Under a Gaussian prior for the base model, our analysis reveals an uncertainty decomposition identity: solicitation depth and assortment breadth are formal substitutes, and total prior uncertainty is a fixed travesty divided between the uncertainty that solicitation eliminates and the uncertainty that tailored assortment breadth hedges. Somewhat surprisingly, the two instruments improve match quality at sharply different rates: expected loss shrinks at a rate of $O(1/m)$ with solicitation depth, whereas tailored assortment breadth suffers a curse of dimensionality, with loss shrinking at the slower rate of $O(k^{-2/d})$. A few well-targeted questions can thus achieve what would otherwise require an exponential number of recommended products. The optimal assortment forms a Voronoi partition, placing each product at the posterior centroid of the candidate ideal positions it targets. For a single-product assortment, the optimal solicitation follows a water-filling rule that equalizes posterior uncertainty across preference dimensions. When multiple products are available, the coordinated optimum can exhibit selective focus, allocating less precision to directions that the assortment can hedge. Moreover, the water-filling policy designed for a single-product assortment admits a general approximation guarantee for larger assortments, with an efficiency gap that vanishes as the preference dimension grows. Beyond the Gaussian case, we show that the uncertainty decomposition identity and the substitutability between solicitation depth and assortment breadth extend to non-Gaussian priors, where the Gaussian model serves as a conservative benchmark and becomes asymptotically exact as the conversation lengthens.

title: Exploring the Signaling Effect of B Corp Certification in Entrepreneurial Finance
affiliations: University of Luxembourg - Interdisciplinary Centre for Security, Reliability and Trust (SnT), University of Trier - Faculty of Management and University of Luxembourg - Interdisciplinary Centre for Security, Reliability and Trust (SnT)

detail.title: Exploring the Signaling Effect of B Corp Certification in Entrepreneurial Finance
detail.abstract: The B Corp certification is the outcome of a voluntary third-party certification process and attests that a venture adheres to certain social and environmental standards. Using propensity score matching on a global dataset of 1,231 B Corp certified ventures and 1,231 comparable non-certified ventures, we examine how an initial B Corp certification influences a venture's likelihood of securing funding from entrepreneurial finance investors. Drawing on signaling theory, we find that the initial adoption of the B Corp certification significantly increases a venture's likelihood of securing funding. We further show that higher B Corp certification scores, indicative of higher signal strength, are more effective in attracting investments. Our findings remain robust when applying an instrumental variables approach, and when considering different types of investments and investors. Notably, our further analyses suggest that the effect of a B Corp certification is especially pronounced for attracting funding from impact investors. Overall, our results provide a nuanced understanding of how signaling and signal strength, through the adoption of a voluntary sustainability standard, influence the funding of entrepreneurial ventures and offer a set of practical implications.

title: AI for Diverse Learners: Teacher Insights from Indian Classrooms

detail.title: AI for Diverse Learners: Teacher Insights from Indian Classrooms

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no financial or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study involved voluntary participation from teachers who shared professional perspectives on the use of artificial intelligence in classrooms. Participants provided informed consent prior to participation. No personal identifying information was collected, and all responses were anonymized. The study followed general ethical principles for educational research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds tremendous promise for transforming K-12 classrooms by supporting students with diverse learning needs, including those with learning differences like ADHD, sensory impairments, and varied language backgrounds common in multilingual India. Over 60% of Indian educators already use AI tools for teaching and management, seeing their value in preparing students for an AI-driven future (Livemint, 2024). Yet, this integration surfaces critical limitations demanding examination. This qualitative study captures authentic teacher insights through semi-structured interviews with 12 experienced K-12 educators from diverse Indian contexts-varying socioeconomic backgrounds, technology access, subjects, and student demographics. Interviews (30-45 minutes) focused on one core objective: analyzing teacher insights on how AI tools support diverse learners and associated limitations/pitfalls. This was explored through two guiding questions addressing content simplification, multilingual access, learning-style customization (auditory, visual, kinaesthetic), and accessible formats alongside technical and emotional challenges. Braun and Clarke's (2006) thematic analysis revealed AI's strengths in boosting confidence and accessibility for below-average and multilingual learners, alongside pitfalls like STEM inaccuracies and over-reliance concerns. The study offers practical recommendations for ethical AI integration-hybrid models combining technology's strengths with teacher empathy.

title: A Prescriptive Analytics Framework for Modeling Product Sequencing in Pharmaceutical Packaging Lines
affiliations: Universidad Iberoamericana, Universidad Iberoamericana, and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Prescriptive Analytics Framework for Modeling Product Sequencing in Pharmaceutical Packaging Lines
detail.abstract: This study formulates the sequencing of pharmaceutical products on packaging lines as a prescriptive analytics problem to enhance operational efficiency in healthcare manufacturing systems. A two-stage optimization framework is developed that integrates descriptive analytics, through similarity-based product clustering, with prescriptive optimization based on a Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) sequencing model to minimize setup times and related inefficiencies. The problem is solved using both an exact optimization approach implemented in Gurobi and a metaheuristic ant system algorithm. The methodology is evaluated on four real-world production lines in a pharmaceutical company, where results show that as product complexity increases, the Ant System achieves solutions comparable to or better than those obtained by the exact solver for full-set sequencing. Clustering products into homogeneous families prior to sequencing yields additional reductions in setup times, underscoring the value of structured segmentation in operational decision-making. Numerical and graphical analyses further reveal stable transition patterns within product families, enabling more standardized and predictable sequencing strategies. Compared with the company’s existing manual scheduling practices, the proposed analytics-driven framework reduces setup times by up to 19.3% and is readily adaptable to other healthcare and life sciences manufacturing environments where setup minimization is critical to operational performance.

title: How Effective was the Japan-US Coordinated Rate Check?
affiliations: Kobe City University of Foreign Studies and Kobe City University of Foreign Studies

detail.title: How Effective was the Japan-US Coordinated Rate Check?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported by the JSPS KAKENHI Grant Numbers 25K05170.

detail.abstract: This paper evaluates the effectiveness of the unprecedented Japan-US coordinated rate check (CRC) conducted on January 23, 2026, as a preparatory action toward implementing foreign exchange (FX) intervention. We first estimate the lasting effect of the CRC using our methodology based on synthetic control methods. We find that the effect of the CRC significantly lasted for 7 business days after the end of the CRC. We then compare the CRC with the four FX intervention events in 2022-24. We find that the power of the lasting effect of the CRC was roughly equivalent to that of the large-scale yen-buying intervention event of April 29 and May 1, 2024. Therefore, despite not actually implementing FX intervention, this coordinated action by the Japanese and US monetary authorities proved effective in correcting the yen’s depreciation against the dollar.

title: Fire or hire as a response to Covid-19? Human and social capital as antecedents of workforce reductions in family firms
affiliations: University of South-Eastern Norway, Bocconi University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Fire or hire as a response to Covid-19? Human and social capital as antecedents of workforce reductions in family firms
detail.abstract: From a resources-based view, this study sheds light on how two different types of family resources, their human and social capital, influenced workforce reductions in family firms during the Covid-19 pandemic. Furthermore, we provide a nuanced understanding of these relationships by exploring the heterogeneity of family firms through the role played by the founding generation. Theoretical hypotheses are tested using global survey data comprising of a final sample of 1,805 observations from 75 different countries. The main findings suggest that while family human capital has a negative impact on the size of the workforce during a crisis, family social capital does not lead to workforce reductions. Moreover, the negative effect that family human capital has on workforce size strengthens when the founding generation of the family is involved. These findings have important implications for understanding the impact of family resources from a resource-based view, providing valuable insights into how resources can be transformed into actions that determine responses to crisis, while underscoring that different generational dynamics impact these responses.

title: Comparative Analysis of Maintenance Optimization Approaches in African Offshore Platforms

detail.title: Comparative Analysis of Maintenance Optimization Approaches in African Offshore Platforms
detail.abstract: Offshore oil and gas platforms operating in Africa face persistent challenges related to high operational expenditure, aging infrastructure, safety risks, and unplanned downtime, all of which are closely linked to maintenance effectiveness. This study conducts a comparative analysis of maintenance optimization approaches applied within African offshore platforms, with particular focus on preventive, reliability-centered, predictive, and digitally enabled maintenance models. Drawing on peer-reviewed literature and documented case insights from African and comparable offshore environments, the study evaluates these approaches using cost efficiency, downtime reduction, safety performance, and contextual feasibility as comparative criteria. The findings indicate that while advanced predictive and AI-driven maintenance systems demonstrate strong potential for cost and downtime reduction, their effectiveness is significantly constrained by infrastructural, data, and skill limitations prevalent in many African offshore contexts. Hybrid maintenance strategies that integrate traditional reliability-centered practices with selective digital tools emerge as the most viable and resilient solution. The study concludes that maintenance optimization in African offshore platforms must prioritize contextual adaptability rather than direct replication of global best practices, and it recommends phased, capacity-aware implementation pathways for sustainable performance improvement (Uke; Joseph; Shamim; Animashaun et al.).

title: From Making to Directing: How AI Creativity Studios Reorganize Creative Labor in Cultural Industries

detail.title: From Making to Directing: How AI Creativity Studios Reorganize Creative Labor in Cultural Industries
detail.abstract: The rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence in cultural and creative industries has intensified debates about whether machines can be considered creative actors. This paper shifts the focus from questions of machine creativity to the organizational transformation of creative work. We argue that contemporary AI creativity studios-software platforms that structure cinematic and visual production through stepwise workflows-reorganize creative labor by transforming human creators from makers into directors of machine-mediated production pipelines. Drawing on an artifact-centered qualitative approach, the study combines walkthrough analysis and decision-rights mapping to examine how creative decisions are distributed across humans, platform workflows, and generative models. Using Higgsfield.ai as a primary empirical exemplar, alongside comparable AI video-generation platforms, we analyze how creative processes are proceduralized, parameterized, and governed through interface design and embedded defaults. Our analysis shows that AI creativity studios do not replace human creativity; rather, they redistribute authorship, agency, and control across socio-technical systems, reshaping creative labor identities and professional boundaries. By conceptualizing AI as an organizational infrastructure for creative production, the paper contributes to research on creative industries, human-AI work arrangements, and innovation management. We conclude by outlining implications for authorship attribution, creative labor governance, and future empirical research on AI-mediated cultural production.

title: Optimizing Maintenance Strategies to Extend Asset Life in Offshore Operations

detail.title: Optimizing Maintenance Strategies to Extend Asset Life in Offshore Operations
detail.abstract: Offshore operations are characterized by harsh environmental conditions, complex mechanical systems, and high operational costs, all of which accelerate asset degradation and shorten equipment lifespan. As offshore infrastructure ages, operators face increasing pressure to maintain reliability, safety, and cost efficiency while extending asset life. This study synthesizes and evaluates optimization-based maintenance strategies applied across offshore oil, gas, wind, and marine operations. Drawing on recent scholarly and industry literature, the study examines preventive, predictive, reliability-centered, and digital twin-enabled maintenance approaches and assesses their effectiveness in extending asset life and improving operational performance. The findings indicate that proactive, data-driven, and probabilistic maintenance strategies significantly outperform traditional time-based approaches in reducing failure rates, minimizing downtime, and optimizing lifecycle costs. However, the study also reveals persistent implementation challenges related to data availability, organizational readiness, and environmental variability. The paper concludes that integrated maintenance optimization frameworks, supported by automation and digital technologies, are essential for sustainable offshore asset management. Future research directions include real-time empirical validation and cross-sector implementation studies to bridge the gap between theoretical optimization models and operational practice (Zhang et al.; Uke; Hendradewa and Yin; Budimir et al.).

title: Integrating Human Factors into Maintenance Strategy Models for Offshore Operations

detail.title: Integrating Human Factors into Maintenance Strategy Models for Offshore Operations
detail.abstract: Offshore operations are complex, high-risk environments that rely heavily on effective maintenance strategies to ensure operational safety, reliability, and sustainability (Uke; Mustafa and Demirel; Bukowski and Werbinska-Wojciechowska). Traditional maintenance optimization models often focus on technical and asset-centered metrics while neglecting critical human factors (Bafandegan Emroozi et al.; Lezdkalne). This study synthesizes contemporary literature on maintenance strategies, human reliability, and offshore safety to explore pathways for integrating human factors into maintenance models. Key findings indicate that human error probability, cognitive workload, fatigue, and organizational culture significantly influence maintenance outcomes. Moreover, conventional models inadequately capture the dynamic interactions between humans, technology, and organizational systems (Melnyk et al.; Song et al.). Integrating human factors into maintenance strategies not only reduces risk but also improves operational efficiency and resilience. The study provides a conceptual framework for combining human reliability insights with maintenance optimization, offering practical implications for offshore operators seeking to enhance safety and performance (Cui et al.; Bukowski and Werbinska-Wojciechowska).

title: Advanced Modeling Techniques for Offshore Oil Platform Reliability and Maintenance

detail.title: Advanced Modeling Techniques for Offshore Oil Platform Reliability and Maintenance
detail.abstract: Offshore oil platforms are vital for global energy supply, but their complex operations are susceptible to equipment failures, structural degradation, and unplanned downtime. This study evaluates advanced modeling techniques including artificial intelligence (AI), Bayesian networks, and digital twin approaches to enhance platform reliability and optimize maintenance strategies. Using a combination of historical operational data, predictive algorithms, and structural simulations, the research demonstrates that integrated modeling significantly reduces maintenance-related downtime and improves decision-making for critical equipment management. Findings indicate that predictive maintenance models outperform traditional preventive strategies in both accuracy and cost-efficiency, while Bayesian network reliability assessments provide robust probabilistic insights. Digital twin implementations enable proactive structural monitoring, highlighting vulnerabilities before failures occur. The study concludes that integrating AI, probabilistic reliability modeling, and digital twin simulation establishes a practical framework for offshore platform maintenance, providing both operational and economic benefits while guiding future research on adaptive predictive models and sensor integration.

title: Innovation Contests and R&D Policy
affiliations: University of Melbourne - Faculty of Business and Economics and University of Melbourne - Faculty of Business and Economics

detail.title: Innovation Contests and R&D Policy
detail.abstract: Innovation contests are widely used for the procurement of innovation. We compare the problem of a private and a public seeker organizing an innovation contest where participants are privately informed about the quality of their ideas. The innovation has to satisfy a predetermined performance threshold to be of use to the seeker. Profit-maximizing seekers underinvest in innovation contests. We investigate how efficiency can be achieved by an R&D policy defined in terms of a matching ratio, which can take, for example, the form of a subsidy or a tax credit. We show that the efficient matching ratio should be lower for more difficult challenges and challenges with a higher number of contestants.

title: Impressions for a Lifetime: Youth Exposure to Immigration and Anti-immigrant Sentiment in Germany
affiliations: University of Essex, Centro Studi Luca d'Agliano (LdA), Università degli Studi di Milano-Bicocca - Department of Economics, Management and Statistics (DEMS) and

detail.title: Impressions for a Lifetime: Youth Exposure to Immigration and Anti-immigrant Sentiment in Germany

publicationDetails.detailsText: University of Milan Bicocca Department of Economics, Management and Statistics Working Paper No. 571
publicationDetails.journalName: University of Milan Bicocca Department of Economics, Management & Statistics Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We examine the impact of exposure to immigrants during formative years on attitudes toward immigration later on in life. Our research design combines granular administrative data on immigrant shares in Germany with longitudinal individual-level data on immigration sentiment. Using panel fixed-effect estimates, identification leverages both spatial variation at critical ages and time variation induced by birth cohorts. We find that individuals exposed to higher shares of immigrants in formative years exhibit more negative attitudes toward immigration in adulthood. The impact is small in magnitude but specific to critical age and robust to contemporaneous immigration exposure. Our findings suggest that early and unmediated exposure to a diverse social and ethnic environment may have long-lasting consequences for the formation of immigration preferences.

title: Attention (And Money) Is All You Need: Why Universities Are Struggling to Keep AI Talent
affiliations: University of Chicago - Department of Economics, University of Chicago, Center for Economic Studies - US Census Bureau and Economic Innovation Group

detail.title: Attention (And Money) Is All You Need: Why Universities Are Struggling to Keep AI Talent
detail.abstract:
We construct a novel dataset linking academic publication records to U.S. Census employer–employee data to track 42,000 AI researchers over two decades. We document systematic changes in the allocation of AI talent. Industry increasingly attracts younger and foreign-born researchers, while gender representation improves more in academia. The top 1% of publishing industry scientists now earn $1.5 million more annually than comparable academics, a fivefold increase since 2001. Rising wage premia coincide with greater sorting into large incumbent firms. Researchers who move to industry publish less but patent more, consistent with a shift from open science toward proprietary innovation.
